what_it_does: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique where an AI model is given access to a large external knowledge base — like a giant library — and fetches relevant passages before answering a question, improving accuracy. As those libraries grow to contain trillions of words, the time spent searching the library starts to dwarf the time spent actually generating the answer. Hermes attacks this by splitting the library across many computers and using a two-step search: a cheap, rough scan first identifies which machines likely hold relevant passages, and only those machines then do the expensive exact search. This means most machines do no work for most queries, dramatically cutting the time and energy spent on retrieval at trillion-token scale.
